read.bigIdea: Made and aged in Scotland, three years minimum.
read.where: **Scotch whisky** is distilled in Scotland and aged in **oak casks of 700 liters or less** in Scotland for at least **three years**. It is bottled at **40% or more**, and any age on the label is the **youngest** whisky in it. Plain caramel color is allowed.

keyPoints.line: is malted barley from one distillery, in pot stills.
means one distillery, not one barrel.
Scotch mixes malt and grain whiskies.

read.bigIdea: Single or blended, malt or grain.
read.where: **Single malt**: 100% malted barley, pot stills, **one distillery**. **Single grain**: one distillery, other grains allowed. **Blended malt**: single malts from **more than one** distillery. **Blended grain**: single grains from more than one. **Blended Scotch**: malt and grain whiskies together, which is most of the Scotch sold.
read.mixup: **Single** means one distillery, not one barrel.

keyPoints.line: smoke comes from drying the malt over a peat fire.
is known for peated, smoky whiskies.

read.bigIdea: Five places the law protects by name.
read.where: The rules protect **Highland**, **Lowland** and **Speyside** as regions and **Islay** and **Campbeltown** as localities. Many **Islay** whiskies are **peated**: the malt is dried over a peat fire, which gives a **smoky** taste. Where a whisky comes from is a clue, not a rule about flavor.

keyPoints.line: only, aged at least three years in wood.
whiskey uses malted and unmalted barley.
pot still, malt, grain and blended.

read.bigIdea: Made in Ireland, aged at least three years.
read.where: **Irish whiskey** is made on the island of Ireland and aged at least **three years** in wood. There are four kinds: **single pot still**, **single malt**, **single grain** and **blended**. **Single pot still** is unique to Ireland: pot stills and a mash of at least **30% malted** and **30% unmalted barley**, which gives a creamy, spicy feel.

stops.name: Single pot still
stops.text: Malted **and unmalted** barley, pot stills, one distillery.

stops.name: Blended
stops.text: A mix of the others; most Irish whiskey sold.

keyPoints.line: standard from Japan’s whisky makers’ association.
minimum, in casks of 700 liters or less.

read.bigIdea: Since 2021, a standard says what “Japanese” means.
read.where: Japan’s whisky makers’ association set a standard in **2021**. To say **Japanese whisky**, members must use grain including malted grain and **water from Japan**, mash, ferment and distill **in Japan**, age at least **three years** in wood casks of **700 liters or less** in Japan, and **bottle in Japan** at 40% or more. It’s the association’s rule, not a law.

keyPoints.line: only: mashed, distilled and aged there.
on a Canadian label can mean little rye.

read.bigIdea: Three years in Canada, often called “rye.”
read.where: **Canadian whisky** is mashed, distilled and aged in **Canada**, in small wood for at least **three years**, and bottled at **40% or more**. It may contain caramel and flavoring. On a Canadian label, **“rye”** and **“Canadian whisky”** mean the same thing, even when there’s little rye in it.
read.mixup: **Canadian “rye”** is a name, not a recipe. **US rye** must be at least 51% rye.

sources: Canada Food and Drug Regulations, Canadian whisky (as summarized on Wikipedia); Irish Whiskey Technical File (2014); Japan Spirits & Liqueur Makers Association, Standards for Labeling Japanese Whisky (2021), as summarized by Nikka (nikka.com); Scotch Whisky Regulations 2009 (legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2009/2890). Checked Nov 8, 2026.

facts.fact: Scotch whisky is distilled in Scotland and aged in oak casks of 700 liters or less in Scotland for at least three years. It is bottled at 40% or more, and any age on the label is the youngest whisky in it. Plain caramel color is allowed.

Single malt: 100% malted barley, pot stills, one distillery. Single grain: one distillery, other grains allowed. Blended malt: single malts from more than one distillery. Blended grain: single grains from more than one. Blended Scotch: malt and grain whiskies together, which is most of the Scotch sold.

The rules protect Highland, Lowland and Speyside as regions and Islay and Campbeltown as localities. Many Islay whiskies are peated: the malt is dried over a peat fire, which gives a smoky taste. Where a whisky comes from is a clue, not a rule about flavor.

Irish whiskey is made on the island of Ireland and aged at least three years in wood. There are four kinds: single pot still, single malt, single grain and blended. Single pot still is unique to Ireland: pot stills and a mash of at least 30% malted and 30% unmalted barley, which gives a creamy, spicy feel.

Japan’s whisky makers’ association set a standard in 2021. To say Japanese whisky, members must use grain including malted grain and water from Japan, mash, ferment and distill in Japan, age at least three years in wood casks of 700 liters or less in Japan, and bottle in Japan at 40% or more. It’s the association’s rule, not a law.
facts.source: Japan Spirits & Liqueur Makers Association, Standards for Labeling Japanese Whisky (2021), as summarized by Nikka (nikka.com)

facts.fact: Canadian whisky is mashed, distilled and aged in Canada, in small wood for at least three years, and bottled at 40% or more. It may contain caramel and flavoring. On a Canadian label, “rye” and “Canadian whisky” mean the same thing, even when there’s little rye in it.
facts.source: Canada Food and Drug Regulations, Canadian whisky (as summarized on Wikipedia)
